answer: Plant canary answers in the grading queue. The network quietly mixes in submissions it already knows are junk, such as text that names saffron and basalt but says nothing coherent. Honest graders score them low. A sybil ring that rubber-stamps its own members tends to approve everything to save effort, so it attests the canaries too. Each wrong pass cuts that grader's weight, and a cluster caught repeatedly is frozen until it rebuilds trust. Fakes can't hide in an ivory tower of mutual praise when the test answers are invisible.
